references.text: During the ninth plague in Egypt, God sent a thick darkness over all the land of Egypt for three days ([ref:2 Mos 10:21-23|Exodus 10:21-23]). The darkness at Jesus' crucifixion reflects this judgmental darkness – God intervenes with supernatural darkness as a sign of judgment.

The prophet Amos speaks of the day of the Lord as "a time of darkness and not light" ([ref:Am 2:2|Amos 2:2]). The darkness over the land at Jesus' death can be seen as a fulfillment of the prophecy concerning the darkness of the day of the Lord.

Amos prophesies: "On that day, says the Lord God, I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight" ([ref:Am 8:9|Amos 8:9]). This is a striking parallel to the darkness that fell over the land from the sixth to the ninth hour – that is, midday.

Joel prophesies that "the sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes" ([ref:Joel 2:31|Joel 2:31]). The darkness at the cross can be understood as a foretaste of the eschatological day of judgment.
Joel describes that "the sun and moon are darkened, and the stars lose their brightness" ([ref:Joel 3:15|Joel 3:15]). Cosmic signs in connection with God's judgment.

Isaiah prophesies that "the stars of heaven and its constellations will not give their light; the sun is dark when it rises, and the moon does not shine" ([ref:Jes 13:10|Isaiah 13:10]). Cosmic darkness as a sign of God's judgment – a motif reflected at Jesus' crucifixion.

The parallel passage in Matthew: "From the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour" ([ref:Matt 27:45|Matthew 27:45]). Matthew's account of the same event with nearly identical wording.

The parallel passage in Mark: "When the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour" ([ref:Mark 15:33|Mark 15:33]). Mark's account of the darkness at the crucifixion.

Zephaniah describes the day of the Lord as "a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness" ([ref:Sef 1:15|Zephaniah 1:15]). Darkness as a sign of God's day of wrath – a theme fulfilled in the darkness over Golgotha.
